top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu, single credited name) is the only proposal that names a writer, and on the common criteria it carries the strongest whole-oeuvre claim I can defend from public knowledge: a distinctive voice in dense, patterned Romanian prose, and formal ambition in the cumulative architecture of Blinding (first volume of the Orbitor trilogy) and Solenoid, where memory, the body, dream and cosmology form one imaginative system, with real intellectual depth. The citation should be scoped to the prose project, with the poetry named only as its origin, since poetry and early fiction are the most unevenly translated strands. The ballot does not rest on the unanimous support in round 2, on fame, or on national symbolism. The reservations are evidential: I have not read the works, the effect depends on Romanian rhythm and density that I can judge only through translation, and no Romanian-language expert input is documented. It remains unresolved whether the later long works enlarge the project or restate its motifs. Adonis remains the strongest alternative on formal and linguistic renewal of a poetic language, but he is not a proposal on this slate. P000 is ranked last because nothing in the supplied evidence makes no award preferable to a laureate whose case survives these reservations.
recusal_note: none apparent from the profile; my scholarly work on Celan, the fragment, exile literature and Ekelöf is context rather than evidence of preference, and the profile records no personal or professional tie to Cărtărescu
